note: Traditions built to be moved through rather than read or operated: sequences, thresholds, rooms and reveals. For portfolios, showcases, story surfaces and anything whose job is to be an occasion. It shares the persuade deck's property, that the catalog's flagships are beloved things carrying a time of day and a place you can stand in, and differs in what it asks of them: persuade needs one moment to dominate, experience needs an order that rewards going through it.

bar:
## The experience bar, which is not the bar for other modes

This world will be dealt to portfolios, case studies and story surfaces. Its
job is to be an occasion, which makes it the mode most likely to produce
something beautiful and most likely to produce something empty.

**Name the order.** An experience world has a first thing, a threshold and a
reward. Say what the surface does before anything is understood, what marks
the crossing, and what going further buys. A world that is only an atmosphere
has no order, and the catalog's record on that is unambiguous: the atmosphere
tier converts at 12% against 37% for interaction, and every rejection that read
"too abstract" or "doesn't translate" was a mood without a sequence.

**Motion is allowed to matter here.** In the other modes motion is trim. Here
it can be the mechanism, but state it as a law rather than a flourish: what
moves, against what, and what it costs a reader who arrives with motion
reduced. A world whose whole idea disappears under a reduced-motion setting has
one idea and no system.

**It still has to be a system.** The temptation in this mode is a single
unrepeatable set piece. Your five rules must dress a second page, an index, an
about page, a 404. The judged transfers were emphatic on this: a style is
applied, a world generates. Name what your identity does on a surface it was
never designed for and did not want.

**What earns a flagship here.** The same property as persuade, since these two
modes are what the catalog's 102 three-star worlds are mostly made of: a time
of day, a place you can stand in, and a subculture that loved it. Put that in
the spark and let it drive the material.
